notes.summary: Geometry is the biggest Advanced Maths topic: 2–4 questions in Tier 1 and 3–5 in Tier 2. Most questions use a handful of triangle and circle theorems. Figures are not to scale; trust the given values.

concepts.title: Triangle angles
concepts.body: Angles of a triangle add to 180°. An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

concepts.title: Circle theorems
concepts.body:
• Angle at the centre = 2 × angle at the circumference on the same arc.
  • Angle in a semicircle = 90°.
  • Radius ⟂ tangent at the point of contact; two tangents from an outside point are equal.

concepts.title: Similarity and proportional segments
concepts.body: Basic Proportionality Theorem: if DE ∥ BC in ΔABC, then AD/DB = AE/EC. Angle bisector theorem: if AD bisects ∠A, then BD/DC = AB/AC. In similar triangles, areas are in the ratio of the squares of sides.

varieties.name: Angles in triangles
varieties.how: Use angle sum 180° and the exterior angle property.

example.q: In ΔABC, ∠A = 60° and ∠B = 45°. Find the exterior angle at C.

varieties.name: Circle theorems
varieties.how: Spot the theorem: centre angle, semicircle, or tangent ⟂ radius (then use Pythagoras).

example.q: A tangent from a point 10 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 6 cm. Tangent length?

varieties.name: BPT and angle bisector
varieties.how: Set up the ratio of segments and cross-multiply.

example.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = 2, DB = 3, AE = 4. Find EC.

tips: Mark the right angles first: semicircle, tangent–radius, altitude.
traps: The angle at the circumference is half the centre angle only when both stand on the same arc.
In BPT, compare AD/DB with AE/EC, not AD/AB with AE/EC (both work, but do not mix them).

questions.q: In the given figure, ∠BAC = 50° and ∠ABC = 70°. Side BC is extended to D. What is ∠ACD?
In the given figure, AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O and C is a point on the circle. If ∠CAB = 35°, what is ∠CBA?
In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 4 cm, DB = 6 cm and AE = 6 cm, find EC.
questions.solution:
By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, AD/DB = AE/EC.
4/6 = 6/EC → EC = 36/4 = 9 cm.

questions.q: A point P is 13 cm from the centre O of a circle of radius 5 cm. What is the length of the tangent PT drawn from P to the circle?
In the given figure, O is the centre of the circle and ∠AOB = 110°. C is a point on the major arc. What is ∠ACB?
questions.solution:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc AB.
∠ACB = 110°/2 = 55°.

questions.q: In ΔABC, AD is the bisector of ∠A meeting BC at D. If AB = 6 cm, AC = 9 cm and BC = 10 cm, find BD.
questions.solution:
Angle bisector theorem: BD/DC = AB/AC = 6/9 = 2/3.
BD = 10 × 2/(2 + 3) = 4 cm.
